summary: Lay out six mounted trial lenses inside a hexagonal base. Check slot clearance at the angled walls, label visibility and rim-only handling.
intro: Six sides do not automatically make room for six lenses. Near the angled walls a parallel row can run out of width before a lens rim clears the lid. sections: Find the narrowest section of the hexagon

Draw the finished internal outline after board and wrap allowances. At each proposed slot draw the largest mounted lens and handle in the approved orientation. The middle row may fit while the end positions interfere with a corner. Compare a staggered row with a larger footprint; the first changes how labels read, the second changes carton utilisation.
Read the label before taking out the lens

Ask the owner to supply the six identifiers exactly as they should appear. OCULUS documents multiple lens groups and optional modules in its larger trial sets. A six-piece demonstration selection needs its own contents list. With the case on a desk, ask a second person to identify one specified piece and lift it by its approved contact area without moving its neighbours.
Approve the rim support and the lid together

Trial the thickest rim and the smallest rim rather than sizing every groove to an average. Inspect for contact on the optical surface and test whether the lid disturbs the handle position. Mark the intended front on the inner tray and the base. On the illustrated hinged case, check the rear row as the lid sweeps open. Place the tallest handle there for the clearance trial and record the angle at which a user can lift it free.

Fold the roll ends, install the divider and load the components in the proposed bench sequence. Watch the leading edge of each locking wing as the lid closes. Keep the lid from acting as a wrench

A deep slip lid may turn slightly as it comes off. On a surrogate mark the angular position of the tray, close the box, then remove the lid as a recipient would. Lift it as the recipient would

A pull tab at one end can tip the instrument toward the opposite wall. Try the full upper tray with two hands and then with one hand while the box sits on a counter. HEINE lists several otoscope kits with different handle and charging options. Ask for the exact sellable configuration and its packed photographs. Close one door and then the other on the loaded dummy. A centre gap that changes when the instrument is removed points to a clearance problem; one that remains calls for a hinge and wrap inspection. Choose a bay based on the pouch variation

A close recess gives a tidy display for one stable pouch size. A broader compartment with a removable retaining card can accommodate approved alternatives, provided it does not pinch a seal or obscure identification. Ask a person unfamiliar with the packing layout to identify the sensor model and remove the bag without tugging the lead. A visually straight probe does not establish calibration status. The device owner should specify receipt checks and any required verification before use. Give the connector a parking place

The connector can swing back towards the head even when the handle stays seated. Try the complete packout with the cable relaxed. Compare a separate pocket with a removable cable divider: the pocket simplifies counting, while the divider may accommodate another cable length without changing the head cradle. Reject a layout that relies on pushing the connector under the probe.
Check the lid with the paperwork installed

Load the approved protective cover, cable and actual document pouch. Close the lid without pressing it down and reopen it. Inspect for displacement and ask the device team to check face clearance with a suitable surrogate. For clinic-to-clinic transport follow the original equipment instructions and any specified case. title: Two Tea Tins and a Scoop Gift Box: Plan the Insert and Packout
seoTitle: Two Tea Tins and Scoop Gift Box Insert | MTT
summary: Two sealed tins and a scoop need three separate decisions: how the tins are supported, where the scoop can be lifted, and how the filled assembly closes and travels.
intro: Two sealed tins and a scoop need three separate decisions: how the tins are supported, where the scoop can be lifted, and how the filled assembly closes and travels. Measure the finished tins with lids and labels and provide the scoop in its intended protective wrapper. A book-style box can display the complete set, but real fit, closure and transport performance must be checked on representative samples.
cta: Send filled component dimensions, quantity per design and destination for a packaging review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Start with the finished tin, not nominal tea weight

A tin described as holding 50 g of tea does not establish its actual diameter or height. Measure the widest closed tin, lid projection and any seam or label, and record its filled weight. Include the range if two suppliers or tin sizes will be used. Note which decorated surfaces cannot tolerate rubbing. Agree whether both tins can use one cavity size; a common cavity may simplify assembly but still needs a fit check for the smallest tin.
Decide how each tin is supported and removed

A snug circular opening can position the tin for presentation while leaving insufficient space for a finger. Consider a finger recess, a suitable lift tab or a removable tray, then test with the heaviest and lightest filled tin. Support should be assessed around the body and beneath the base rather than relying on the lid or a fragile label. Record where the buyer should grip and whether the second tin stays seated during removal.
Give the scoop its own wrapped position

Measure the complete scoop including any sleeve, tie or guard. A shallow channel can make the tool visible; a covered pocket may suit a loose or flexible accessory but adds a separate removal step. Check that the scoop cannot press against the box cover or tin, and agree who supplies and inserts it. The illustration is a design concept: it does not establish a food-contact approval or a completed manufacturing project.
Separate presentation from food contact and shipping

This presentation box assumes the tea remains in separately sealed primary packaging. If the scoop or an inner material touches tea directly, request the relevant material declaration for the actual use and destination market; do not infer suitability from a generic food-safe label. The US FDA explanation of food-contact substances describes why the material and intended use matter. Distribution risk is another decision: specify the outer shipper and evaluate the complete packed set for its route. ISTA advises reassessing tests when product, packaging or process changes may affect performance.
Make the quotation and sample comparable

Send closed-tin drawings, filled weights, photos of lids and labels, the wrapped scoop, quantity by artwork, target market, packing location and delivery route. Ask for the box, insert and optional bag or card as separate line items, with sampling and freight shown separately. Compare the separate-lid tea tin box against this book-style set with scoop channel using the same contents and outer-pack scope. For custom production, the starting quantity is 1,000 pieces per design and the minimum product value is US$2,000 per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.

imageAlt: Illustrative customizable packaging concept, not a finished customer order
title: Drip Coffee Sachet Drawer Box: Size Dividers for Real Packout
seoTitle: Drip Coffee Sachet Drawer Divider Fit | MTT
summary: A divided drawer should hold the actual sealed sachets without forcing seals, allow a customer to remove one and slide smoothly when loaded.
intro: A divided drawer should hold the actual sealed sachets without forcing seals, allow a customer to remove one and slide smoothly when loaded. Measure the filled sachets across their full width, seal margins and thickness range, not just the flat artwork. Compare divider layout, card position and packout order with real components before approving the sample.
cta: Send filled component dimensions, quantity per design and destination for a packaging review. Minimum 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees.
sections: Measure the filled and sealed pack

A flat dieline misses the thickness created by the coffee and filter inside. Collect representative filled sachets across the product range, including the widest seal and any tear notch. Measure the height, overall width and thickness in the intended orientation. Record how many sachets go in each compartment, since a stack behaves differently from one packet. Do not assume an unfilled artwork proof demonstrates fit.
Balance presentation and removal

A separate paperboard divider can hold flavors in order, but dividers consume internal width and can lean or catch flexible seals. Check the narrowest and widest sealed packets in each compartment. A finger recess or open top may help access, but must not expose fragile seals to lid pressure. Agree the selection order and check that removing one sachet does not displace the rest. Compare the single-layer divided drawer concept with the existing two-drawer arrangement.
Place the information card outside the crush path

Measure the card or folded leaflet as supplied, including any envelope. A dedicated end slot keeps it visible, but it should not push the adjacent sachet or prevent the drawer closing. Mark the front orientation and whether the packer inserts the card before or after the sachets. If several languages or editions are in use, the packing instruction needs a version check; the illustration is not evidence of a finished customer project.
Test the drawer when it is loaded

The empty tray may slide well while the filled set catches at the sleeve entrance or bows at the base. Load the specified number and heaviest sachet combination, check the opening force by hand, and look for snagged seals, bowed dividers and contact between tray contents and sleeve. Repeat with actual samples and the intended outer shipping pack; agree acceptance criteria for displacement and damage rather than claiming a universal clearance.
Clarify food-contact and quote scope

The concept holds individually sealed coffee packs; the decorative outer box is not claimed to provide a food barrier. Where any component directly contacts food, request suitable evidence for its use and destination. See the FDA overview of food-contact substances. Give MTT finished sachet samples, quantity and flavor mix, card dimensions, artwork, packing site and destination. Ask for box, divider, optional accessories, sampling and freight separately. Custom projects start at 1,000 pieces per design and US$2,000 product value per order, excluding freight, samples and other fees. Review the transport approach with reference to ISTA guidance on changes and retesting.
